metadata.purpose: Comprehensive test plan for validating the Configure AlertManager Operator functionality, covering installation, configuration, monitoring, and troubleshooting across OpenShift environments
metadata.target_audience: SRE Engineers, QE Team, Platform Engineers
learning_objectives: Understand how CAMO dynamically configures Alertmanager based on secrets and configmaps
Learn the relationship between secrets (PagerDuty, GoAlert, DMS) and Alertmanager routing
Master troubleshooting techniques for Alertmanager configuration issues
Validate metrics and alerts exposed by CAMO
Practice safe testing with backup/cleanup patterns for state-modifying operations

learning_path.description: Progressive learning path from basic installation validation to advanced troubleshooting

required_access.name: OpenShift Cluster Admin Access
required_access.purpose: Required to create/modify secrets and configmaps in openshift-monitoring namespace
required_access.how_to_get: Request cluster-admin role from cluster administrator
required_access.verification: oc auth can-i create secrets -n openshift-monitoring

required_access.name: Cluster Monitoring Access
required_access.purpose: View Prometheus metrics and Alertmanager configuration
required_access.verification: oc auth can-i get prometheuses -n openshift-monitoring

tools.name: jq
tools.install: brew install jq (macOS) or apt-get install jq (Linux)

camo_operator.title: Configure AlertManager Operator (CAMO)
camo_operator.description: CAMO is a Kubernetes operator that watches for secrets and configmaps in openshift-monitoring namespace and dynamically updates Alertmanager configuration based on their presence or absence. It enables GitOps-friendly alert routing to PagerDuty, GoAlert, and Dead Man's Snitch.
camo_operator.why_it_matters: CAMO eliminates manual Alertmanager configuration management. When you create a pd-secret, CAMO automatically configures PagerDuty routing. Delete the secret, and routing is automatically removed. This makes alert configuration declarative and prevents configuration drift.

alertmanager_config.title: Alertmanager Configuration Secret
alertmanager_config.description: Alertmanager configuration is stored in a Secret named 'alertmanager-main' in the openshift-monitoring namespace. The secret contains an 'alertmanager.yaml' key with the full routing configuration.
alertmanager_config.why_it_matters: Understanding how Alertmanager config is stored is crucial for troubleshooting. CAMO reads this secret, modifies the YAML, validates it, and writes it back. Invalid configs are rejected to prevent Alertmanager failures.

config_validation.title: Alertmanager Configuration Validation
config_validation.description: CAMO validates all configuration changes using Alertmanager's official config.Load() function before writing to the secret. This prevents invalid configurations from breaking Alertmanager.
config_validation.why_it_matters: Invalid Alertmanager configs cause Alertmanager pods to crash-loop. CAMO's validation prevents this by rejecting bad configs and exposing a metric (alertmanager_config_validation_failed) to monitor validation status.

pagerduty_integration.title: PagerDuty Integration
pagerduty_integration.description: CAMO configures PagerDuty routing when a secret named 'pd-secret' exists with key 'PAGERDUTY_KEY' containing a PagerDuty integration key. Alerts from managed namespaces are routed to PagerDuty automatically.
pagerduty_integration.why_it_matters: PagerDuty is the primary escalation path for critical alerts. Understanding how CAMO configures PagerDuty routing helps troubleshoot missing or duplicate pages.

goalert_integration.title: GoAlert Integration
goalert_integration.description: CAMO configures GoAlert routing when 'goalert-secret' exists with keys GOALERT_URL_HIGH, GOALERT_URL_LOW, and GOALERT_HEARTBEAT. High-priority alerts page, low-priority alerts notify without paging.
goalert_integration.why_it_matters: GoAlert provides alert routing with severity-based escalation. High/low separation reduces alert fatigue while ensuring critical issues still page on-call engineers.

dms_integration.title: Dead Man's Snitch Integration
dms_integration.description: CAMO configures Dead Man's Snitch routing when 'dms-secret' exists with key 'SNITCH_URL' containing a DMS webhook URL. This enables cluster heartbeat monitoring - if Alertmanager stops sending heartbeats, DMS pages.
dms_integration.why_it_matters: Dead Man's Snitch detects complete monitoring failures. If the entire monitoring stack goes down, DMS will page because it stopped receiving heartbeats.

cluster_readiness.title: Cluster Readiness Check (osd-cluster-ready)
cluster_readiness.description: CAMO waits for the 'osd-cluster-ready' Job to complete before configuring PagerDuty. This prevents alert noise during cluster installation when many components are starting up.
cluster_readiness.why_it_matters: New clusters fire many alerts during installation. Delaying PagerDuty configuration until the cluster is ready prevents unnecessary pages to on-call engineers.

system_impact.description: Only queries cluster resources to verify CAMO deployment status

objectives: Verify CAMO operator is deployed and running
Understand operator deployment patterns in OpenShift
skills_gained: Check operator deployment status using oc commands

test_execution.objective: Validate that CAMO operator is installed, running, and managed by OLM

steps.title: Verify CAMO deployment exists and is available
steps.learning_note: Deployments manage the operator pod. An available deployment means the operator is running.
steps.why_this_step: Confirms the operator deployment exists and has the desired number of replicas running

common_errors.error: Error from server (NotFound): deployments.apps "configure-alertmanager-operator" not found
common_errors.solution: CAMO operator is not installed. Check if OLM has installed the operator or install manually.

steps.title: Check CAMO pod is running
steps.learning_note: The actual operator process runs inside a pod. Pod should be in Running state with no restarts.
steps.why_this_step: Verifies the operator pod is healthy and not crash-looping

common_errors.solution: Check pod logs: oc logs -n openshift-monitoring deployment/configure-alertmanager-operator

steps.title: Verify ClusterServiceVersion (CSV) exists and succeeded
steps.learning_note: CSV is how OLM tracks operator installation. Succeeded status means OLM successfully installed and is managing the operator.
steps.why_this_step: Confirms OLM has successfully installed and is managing the CAMO operator

success_criteria: Pod is in Running state with 1/1 containers ready
validation.how_to_verify: Run: oc get deployment,pod,csv -n openshift-monitoring -l name=configure-alertmanager-operator
validation.what_success_means: CAMO operator is installed, running, and being managed by OLM correctly
validation.what_failure_means: Operator is not installed, not running, or OLM is not managing it properly. Check OLM logs and CSV status.

common_failures.symptom: Deployment exists but pod keeps restarting
common_failures.cause: Operator failing to start, likely due to RBAC issues or invalid configuration
debug_steps: Check pod logs: oc logs -n openshift-monitoring deployment/configure-alertmanager-operator
Check for RBAC errors in logs
Verify ServiceAccount exists: oc get sa configure-alertmanager-operator -n openshift-monitoring
common_failures.fix: Review logs for specific error, check RBAC permissions
common_failures.prevention: Ensure OLM has properly installed all RBAC resources

getting_help: Check operator logs: oc logs -n openshift-monitoring deployment/configure-alertmanager-operator
Check OLM logs: oc logs -n openshift-operator-lifecycle-manager deployment/olm-operator
Review CSV status: oc describe csv -n openshift-monitoring

next_steps.on_success: Proceed to test_verify_rbac to validate operator permissions
bonus_exploration: Explore CSV details: oc get csv -n openshift-monitoring -o yaml
Check operator version: oc get deployment configure-alertmanager-operator -n openshift-monitoring -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'

system_impact.description: Reads alertmanager-main secret and displays configuration - makes no changes

objectives: Understand how Alertmanager configuration is stored in Kubernetes
Learn to extract and read YAML from secrets
Identify receivers and routes in Alertmanager config
skills_gained: Extract and decode base64-encoded secret data

test_execution.objective: Read and inspect the current Alertmanager configuration managed by CAMO

steps.title: Verify alertmanager-main secret exists
steps.learning_note: Alertmanager configuration is stored in a Secret, not a ConfigMap. This allows Prometheus Operator to reload Alertmanager when config changes.
steps.why_this_step: Confirms the secret exists before attempting to read it

steps.title: Extract and display alertmanager.yaml from secret
steps.learning_note: Secrets store data base64-encoded. The -o jsonpath extracts the alertmanager.yaml key and base64 decodes it.
steps.command: oc get secret alertmanager-main -n openshift-monitoring -o jsonpath='{.data.alertmanager\.yaml}' | base64 -d
steps.why_this_step: Retrieves the actual Alertmanager YAML configuration

steps.title: List all receivers in the configuration
steps.learning_note: Receivers define WHERE alerts are sent (PagerDuty, GoAlert, DMS, etc.). CAMO dynamically adds/removes receivers based on secrets.
steps.command: oc get secret alertmanager-main -n openshift-monitoring -o jsonpath='{.data.alertmanager\.yaml}' | base64 -d | yq eval '.receivers[].name' -
steps.why_this_step: Shows which alert destinations are currently configured

steps.title: Check if PagerDuty receiver exists
steps.learning_note: If pd-secret exists, CAMO should have created a 'pagerduty' receiver. This command checks if it's present.
steps.command: oc get secret alertmanager-main -n openshift-monitoring -o jsonpath='{.data.alertmanager\.yaml}' | base64 -d | yq eval '.receivers[] | select(.name == "pagerduty")' -
steps.why_this_step: Validates that CAMO configured PagerDuty routing if pd-secret exists

success_criteria: alertmanager.yaml key is present and decodable
validation.how_to_verify: Extract config and validate with yq: oc get secret alertmanager-main -n openshift-monitoring -o jsonpath='{.data.alertmanager\.yaml}' | base64 -d | yq eval . -
validation.what_success_means: Alertmanager configuration is present and readable
validation.what_failure_means: Secret is missing or corrupted. CAMO may not have reconciled yet or encountered errors.

getting_help: Check CAMO logs: oc logs -n openshift-monitoring deployment/configure-alertmanager-operator
Verify secret was created: oc describe secret alertmanager-main -n openshift-monitoring

next_steps.on_success: Proceed to test_create_pagerduty_secret to test dynamic configuration
bonus_exploration: Examine full config structure with yq
Compare receivers section before and after creating secrets

metadata.name: test_create_pagerduty_secret
metadata.title: Create PagerDuty Secret for Alert Routing

system_impact.description: Creates pd-secret in openshift-monitoring namespace, which triggers CAMO to reconfigure Alertmanager

safety.warning_message: ⚠️ This test creates a PagerDuty secret that will cause CAMO to reconfigure Alertmanager. Alerts may start routing to the test PagerDuty key. Run cleanup test afterward to remove.

objectives: Understand how CAMO watches secrets to trigger reconciliation
Learn the structure of pd-secret and required keys
Observe automatic Alertmanager reconfiguration when secret is created
skills_gained: Create secrets with specific keys using oc create secret
Trigger operator reconciliation by creating watched resources
Verify operator reactions to resource changes

test_execution.objective: Create pd-secret and verify CAMO automatically adds PagerDuty receiver to Alertmanager configuration
prerequisites: cluster-admin or ability to create secrets in openshift-monitoring
Test PagerDuty integration key (use TEST_KEY_CHANGEME for testing)

steps.title: Verify pd-secret does NOT exist (clean state)
steps.learning_note: Before creating a secret, verify it doesn't already exist to ensure we're testing CAMO's create behavior.
steps.why_this_step: Ensures clean starting state - if secret exists, delete it first or skip this test

steps.title: Create pd-secret with test PagerDuty key
steps.learning_note: CAMO looks for a secret named 'pd-secret' with key 'PAGERDUTY_KEY'. When created, CAMO's watch triggers reconciliation.
steps.command: oc create secret generic pd-secret --from-literal=PAGERDUTY_KEY=TEST_KEY_CHANGEME -n openshift-monitoring
steps.why_this_step: Creates the secret that CAMO watches, triggering automatic Alertmanager reconfiguration

common_errors.error: Error from server (AlreadyExists): secrets "pd-secret" already exists
common_errors.solution: Secret already exists. Delete it first: oc delete secret pd-secret -n openshift-monitoring, or use --dry-run=client to test the command

common_errors.error: Error from server (Forbidden): secrets is forbidden
common_errors.solution: You lack permissions to create secrets in openshift-monitoring. Request cluster-admin role.

steps.title: Wait for CAMO to reconcile (30-60 seconds)
steps.learning_note: Operator watches are eventually consistent. CAMO needs time to detect the new secret, reconcile, and update alertmanager-main.
steps.why_this_step: Gives CAMO time to detect the secret and update Alertmanager configuration

steps.title: Verify CAMO added PagerDuty receiver to Alertmanager config
steps.learning_note: After reconciliation, alertmanager-main secret should now contain a 'pagerduty' receiver configured with the routing key from pd-secret.
steps.command: oc get secret alertmanager-main -n openshift-monitoring -o jsonpath='{.data.alertmanager\.yaml}' | base64 -d | yq eval '.receivers[] | select(.name == "pagerduty")' -
steps.why_this_step: Confirms CAMO successfully added PagerDuty receiver to Alertmanager configuration

steps.title: Check pd_secret_exists metric is 1
steps.learning_note: CAMO exposes metrics for monitoring. pd_secret_exists should be 1 when pd-secret exists, 0 when absent.
steps.command: oc exec -n openshift-monitoring deployment/configure-alertmanager-operator -- curl -s localhost:8080/metrics | grep 'pd_secret_exists'
steps.why_this_step: Validates CAMO's internal state matches the actual secret presence

success_criteria: No errors in CAMO operator logs
validation.how_to_verify: Check receiver exists: oc get secret alertmanager-main -n openshift-monitoring -o jsonpath='{.data.alertmanager\.yaml}' | base64 -d | yq eval '.receivers[].name' -
validation.what_success_means: CAMO successfully detected pd-secret and reconfigured Alertmanager to route alerts to PagerDuty
validation.what_failure_means: CAMO failed to reconcile. Check operator logs for errors. Secret may have wrong key name or CAMO may not have RBAC permissions.

common_failures.symptom: Secret created but pagerduty receiver not in config after 2 minutes
common_failures.cause: CAMO reconciliation failed or operator is not running
debug_steps: Check CAMO pod is running: oc get pods -n openshift-monitoring -l name=configure-alertmanager-operator
Check CAMO logs for errors: oc logs -n openshift-monitoring deployment/configure-alertmanager-operator --tail=50
Verify secret has correct key: oc get secret pd-secret -n openshift-monitoring -o jsonpath='{.data.PAGERDUTY_KEY}'
common_failures.fix: Review logs for specific error, ensure secret has PAGERDUTY_KEY key (not pagerduty_key or other variations)
common_failures.prevention: Always check operator logs after creating secrets to confirm reconciliation succeeded

getting_help: Check CAMO logs: oc logs -n openshift-monitoring deployment/configure-alertmanager-operator
Verify secret structure: oc get secret pd-secret -n openshift-monitoring -o yaml
Check CAMO metrics: oc exec -n openshift-monitoring deployment/configure-alertmanager-operator -- curl -s localhost:8080/metrics

next_steps.on_success: ⚠️ CLEANUP REQUIRED: Run test_cleanup_pagerduty_secret to remove the test secret and restore Alertmanager config
bonus_exploration: Examine the complete pagerduty receiver config with yq
Watch CAMO logs during reconciliation: oc logs -f -n openshift-monitoring deployment/configure-alertmanager-operator

system_impact.description: Deletes pd-secret, which triggers CAMO to remove PagerDuty receiver from Alertmanager config
affected_resources: Secret: alertmanager-main (modified by CAMO to remove PagerDuty receiver)

objectives: Understand how deleting secrets triggers CAMO reconciliation
Learn cleanup procedures for test resources
Verify system returns to original state after cleanup

test_execution.objective: Remove pd-secret and verify CAMO automatically removes PagerDuty receiver from Alertmanager

steps.title: Verify pd-secret exists before deletion
steps.learning_note: Always verify a resource exists before attempting to delete it to avoid confusion.
steps.why_this_step: Confirms the secret we're about to delete actually exists

steps.title: Delete pd-secret
steps.learning_note: Deleting the secret triggers CAMO to reconcile and remove PagerDuty configuration from Alertmanager.
steps.why_this_step: Removes the test secret, triggering CAMO to clean up PagerDuty routing

steps.title: Wait for CAMO to reconcile
steps.why_this_step: Gives CAMO time to detect deletion and update Alertmanager

steps.title: Verify PagerDuty receiver removed from Alertmanager config
steps.learning_note: After cleanup, the pagerduty receiver should be gone. Only the default 'null' receiver should remain.
steps.command: oc get secret alertmanager-main -n openshift-monitoring -o jsonpath='{.data.alertmanager\.yaml}' | base64 -d | yq eval '.receivers[] | select(.name == "pagerduty")' -
steps.why_this_step: Confirms CAMO removed PagerDuty receiver, restoring original configuration

steps.title: Verify pd_secret_exists metric is 0
steps.command: oc exec -n openshift-monitoring deployment/configure-alertmanager-operator -- curl -s localhost:8080/metrics | grep 'pd_secret_exists'
steps.why_this_step: Confirms CAMO's internal state reflects secret deletion

success_criteria: Pagerduty receiver removed from Alertmanager config
validation.how_to_verify: List all receivers: oc get secret alertmanager-main -n openshift-monitoring -o jsonpath='{.data.alertmanager\.yaml}' | base64 -d | yq eval '.receivers[].name' -
validation.what_success_means: Cleanup successful - system returned to original state before test
validation.what_failure_means: Cleanup failed - secret deleted but Alertmanager config not updated. Check CAMO logs.

getting_help: Check CAMO logs: oc logs -n openshift-monitoring deployment/configure-alertmanager-operator --tail=50

next_steps.on_success: ✅ Cleanup complete. Proceed to test_create_goalert_secret to test GoAlert integration
